newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 29.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 29.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$17.38 (-0.08)

BHP is expected to announce later on Tuesday the results of its year-long steel review, including the rationalisation of its Newcastle steel-making operations. The Australian newspaper said the review would also announce the planned closure of BHP's Port Kembla steel plant by 2020. Newspapers also reported BHP was close to a decision on the sale of its 37 percent Foster's Brewing Group stake. Options include a part Foster's buy-back and a sale to institutional investors.

The deal between EchoStar Communications Corp and News Corp Ltd to build a direct-TV satellite hit a snag Monday, seemingly over an issue analysts said was the least of the venture's worries. EchoStar issued a statement early Monday saying News Corp's planned $1 billion investment was delayed over News Corp's request to abandon its existing conditional-access system.

Hollywood studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc. Monday announced plans to acquire Metromedia International Group Inc.'s entertainment group and film library for US$573 million in cash. The deal, which had been expected for over a week, would expand MGM's catalog to more than 3,800 films that it can market to basic television and home video as well as emerging formats in satellite TV, digital video disks and computer CD-ROMs.

Engineering group Australian National Industries Ltd said on Monday it will have to wait several weeks before a final decision will be made on the report into its acquisition of German environmental business ABT.
MIM Holdings Ltd said on Monday that base metals output in the third quarter ended March 31 was lower due to wet weather at Mount Isa and operations elsewhere in the state of Queensland.
